one_month_reasoning: Effective start is the $64.85 after-hours quote (-5.6%) following the Q3 print: revenue in line, but Q4 EPS guide $0.67 vs $0.73 consensus (includes ~120bps headcount charge), 2026 ad revenue cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B and FCF guide to $12.0B from $12.5B. In the window: the Oct 21 regular-session reaction (after-hours moves are noisy, so I add ~3% of day-one uncertainty), estimate cuts over the following days, the Oct 27-28 FOMC (hold ~87% on Kalshi/Polymarket, hike ~13%), Spotify results Oct 22, and the 10-Q. Post-earnings-announcement drift after a negative guide is a mild negative, a sharp move often partially reverses; net I centre the median at ~$64.5 (slightly below the after-hours price) with a lognormal sigma of 11.5% (37% annual vol / 3.5 = 10.6%, plus day-one noise). P(close >= $68.69 pre-print level) ~29%.

fair_value.method: Engine blend: driver DCF $67.07 (weight 0.2; regional members x ARM build, 31.5%->36.5% EBIT margin, WACC 9.4%, g 3.0%) and 18x NTM GAAP P/E on model EPS at the horizon = $76.09 (weight 0.8), with a -$0.8B probability-weighted M&A adjustment -> $74.28.

Trading there would most likely mean earnings themselves are breaking (paid-member losses after price rises, an ad business that stalls, or margins reversing on sports-rights/content inflation), not a multiple wobble; it is also ~31% below the after-hours price, beyond a one-sigma 12-month move.

key_uncertainties: Engagement: total view hours grew only ~2% in H1 2026 and Netflix's share of US TV time fell to 7.9% while YouTube rose to 13.5%; whether pricing power survives slower engagement.
Ad business trajectory: 2026 cut from ~$3B to ~$2.7B; 2027 ($4B in my base) depends on ad-tech rollout and 15 new ad-tier markets.

Rates: 10y at 5.12% and a priced December hike compress long-duration multiples; recession odds for 2027 ~20% on Kalshi.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine: the 18x NTM P/E implies an 8.7% WACC on my driver path (revenue ~10.7% in 2027 fading to 6-10% by region in 2030, EBIT margin to 36.5%, 3.0% terminal growth). At my 9.4% WACC the same 18x needs about 3.8% growth after 2030 (engine: g 3.8% gives a DCF of $75.9) or a mature margin above ~41% (39.5% gives only $72.8). Plausible but not conservative: it requires Netflix to keep raising prices and growing ads while YouTube gains TV share, which is why I do not pay the 22.45x peer median and why the long-dated engagement risk (-$2.8/share probability-weighted) sits in the multiple.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP EBIT and EPS (after SBC, ~1% of revenue) for NFLX and GAAP NTM P/E for peers; share count change of -3.25%/yr is net of buybacks and SBC issuance, so SBC is counted once.

reasoning: Round 2. Start: $64.85 after hours (-5.6% on a soft Q4 guide, ad revenue cut to ~$2.7B, FCF to $12.0B), 17.1x FY2027 consensus EPS $3.80 (Nasdaq/Zacks still pre-print on 2026-10-20). Fundamentals are intact (Q3 revenue +12%, operating margin 34.6%, $4.8B buyback for 63.9M shares), so the debate is the multiple and engagement. Supervisor findings acted on, each re-verified at source: (a) discount rate: 10y UST 5.12% on the Treasury curve; my own weekly regressions give beta 0.92 (2y), 1.04 (3y), 1.105 since 2023, 1.40 (5y, 2022-dominated); I use Blume 1.07 -> WACC 9.4% (from 10.5%); (b) terminal growth 3.0% (from 3.5%), since the old pair were offsetting errors; (c) share change -3.25% (from -3.5%): diluted shares -3.35% y/y in Q3 but buybacks have run above FCF; I stop slightly short of the supervisor's -3.0%; (d) an M&A adjustment I had missed (-$4B x 20%); (e) peer median 22.45x after dropping LYV and putting GOOGL on FY2027 EPS; my round-1 trailing EV/EBITDA median (16.2x) was an arithmetic slip and is now 11.6x. Base rates (my lane): NFLX's own >40% drawdowns (2004-05, 2011-12, 2022, July 2019 miss) were followed by large 12-month rebounds, but those were operating crises fixed visibly; today's fall is a de-rating of a still-growing business, where momentum persistence (Jegadeesh-Titman) is the broader base rate. Event odds: Kalshi 2027 recession ~20%, December FOMC hike priced with the 10y at 5.12%; Kalshi priced Paramount 65% to complete WBD before July 2027 (July 2026), a bigger content rival in my bear case. Alt-data: Nielsen June 2026 NFLX 7.9% of US TV time vs 8.3% a year earlier, YouTube 13.5%. Valuation: regional members x ARM build -> FY2027 revenue ~$56.6B (+10.7%), EBIT 33%, EPS ~$3.75 (consensus $3.80, -1%); DCF $67.1 at 9.4% (w 0.2) and 18x NTM P/E $76.1 (w 0.8) less M&A -> fair value $74.28; scenarios $50.4/$74.3/$98.6 at 25/50/25. Ladder: 87% weight on a lognormal centred at the engine median $73.8 (sigma 0.31) plus 13% on a stress state centred at $50 (sigma 0.30) for an engagement/ads break; overall median ~$70.6 (+9% vs $64.85 effective start), below fair value to respect momentum and post-print estimate cuts; P(>= $69) 53%, P(>= $93) 20%, P(>= $48) 87%. 1-month ladder unchanged (no new information on the window). No option data used.
